name: United States v. Bajakajian
summary: The Court struck down a federal forfeiture of $357,144 as unconstitutionally excessive under the Eighth Amendment, holding that courts must assess whether a punitive forfeiture is grossly disproportionate to the offense committed.
significance: Bajakajian is the Court's leading precedent on what makes a fine 'excessive,' establishing that a fine is unconstitutional if it is grossly disproportionate to the gravity of the offense, a standard whose application in lower courts has been disputed.
